In-house Web engineering

This website: a real-time WebGL system in one file

The problem

An AI engineering studio whose site looked like every other agency template has already lost the argument before a prospect reads a word.

The system

A single self-contained page running a custom WebGL neural environment, scroll-driven storytelling, an interactive AI lab, ROI modelling and an architecture builder — with graceful degradation when WebGL or the CDN is unavailable.

The technology

Three.js with custom GLSL shaders, GSAP ScrollTrigger, canvas 2D rendering, subset variable fonts, quality tiers for low-power devices, and reduced-motion support throughout.

Three.jsGLSLGSAPWebGLCanvasA11y
1File to deploy
0Console errors
3Quality tiers

Measured on this page: no horizontal overflow from 320px to 1920px, and full functionality with scripts blocked.

In-house Applied AI

The AI lab on this page

The problem

Agencies claim AI capability with stock imagery. A prospect has no way to tell who can actually build a working system.

The system

Five working demos running entirely in your browser: an agent that decomposes a task into a plan, document parsing, unstructured-text extraction, content drafting and an automation pipeline simulator. No data leaves the page.

The technology

Deterministic extraction and planning logic, client-side file reading, and an API abstraction layer ready to switch to a server-side model endpoint when one is configured.

Trust & security

How we handle your systems and your data.

Written plainly, with no certifications we don't hold. If your procurement team needs more detail, ask and you'll get specifics in writing.

This websiteOperational
AI labRunning locally
Contact channelsOperational
Data collectionNone on this page

This website

  • Served over HTTPS
  • No analytics, cookies or trackers on this page
  • No form data is stored here — messages open in your own WhatsApp or email client
  • The AI lab processes everything in your browser; files never leave your device
  • No API keys or secrets exist in this page's source

Systems we build for you

  • Secrets in environment variables, never in client-side code
  • Server-side input validation and schema checks on every endpoint
  • Parameterised queries and ORM-level protection against injection
  • Authentication with hashed passwords and expiring sessions
  • Role-based authorization on admin surfaces
  • Rate limiting and abuse protection on public endpoints
  • Upload type, MIME and size validation
  • Security headers and a content security policy
  • Audit logging that excludes secrets and credentials

AI data handling

  • Model calls run server-side, never from the browser
  • The AI provider is configurable per project — you choose it
  • We tell you exactly which data leaves your infrastructure and why
  • Sensitive fields are redacted or excluded from prompts by design
  • Prompts and outputs are logged only where you ask for it
  • No client data is used to train anything

Working together

  • NDA available before you share anything sensitive
  • Ownership and licensing agreed in writing before work starts
  • Access to your systems requested at the minimum level needed
  • Credentials shared through a password manager, never over chat
  • Handover includes documentation, environment setup and access transfer

What we don't claim. Neural Automation does not hold SOC 2, ISO 27001 or any formal security certification, and we won't imply otherwise. We're a small, senior studio — the practices above are what we actually implement, and we'll walk your team through any of them before you commit.

AI project discovery 01 / 10

Step 01

What does your company do?

One or two lines is plenty — industry, what you sell, who buys it.

Step 02

What problem are you trying to solve?

Describe the pain, not the solution. What's slow, expensive, manual or losing you money?

Step 03

What are you looking to build?

Pick everything that applies.

Step 04

What tools and systems are you using today?

CRM, spreadsheets, accounting, WhatsApp, anything. This tells us what we integrate with rather than replace.

Step 05

How many people touch this process?

Step 06

What scale are you expecting?

Step 07

Which market are you serving?

Step 08

Approximate budget?

A range is fine. It changes what we recommend, not whether we reply.

Step 09

When do you need it live?

Step 10

Who should we address this to?

Optional. Used only to personalise the blueprint you're about to see — nothing is sent anywhere from this page.
